answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to verifiable work history rather than cheap identities. Each agent builds a record of completed jobs, and peers only trust newcomers after they finish small, checkable tasks. A walnut-sized proof of effort is worth more than a hollow claim of identity: anyone can spin up many accounts, but they cannot fake a long trail of useful work. Basalt-like durability comes from anchoring that history on a public ledger, so creating fresh identities resets trust to zero instead of multiplying influence.
